title: Chicken Drumstick, Grilled Without Sauce, Skin Not Eaten

content.title: About
content.content: A chicken drumstick grilled without sauce is a lean source of protein. The skin is not eaten, which reduces the fat content. This dish is commonly served in restaurants and homes as part of a healthy diet.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grilling preserves more nutrients compared with deep‑frying.
Chicken drumsticks contain more iron than breast meat because of the dark muscle fibers.
Skipping the skin cuts calories by 30–40 % and lowers saturated fat intake.
In many cultures drumsticks are marinated in spices, but without sauce they retain the meat’s natural flavor.
Proper grilling creates a flavorful crust that enhances taste.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Chicken drumsticks provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Leaving the skin off reduces saturated fat, supporting cardiovascular health.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: Dark meat is a good source of iron and zinc, which aid immune function and metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Drumsticks supply niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The dish does not cause a rapid spike in blood sugar, beneficial for people with diabetes.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C to avoid salmonella.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the drumsticks were pre‑marinated, sodium levels can be high; use minimal added salt.

items.title: Smoke exposure
items.content: Excessive charring creates carcinogenic compounds; grill over moderate heat.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the drumsticks hot, sliced into pieces, with vegetable sides, quinoa, or whole‑grain rice. They are easy to eat without skin using a fork and knife, or added to salads. Optional toppings include fresh herbs, lemon juice, or a light mustard dressing.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked drumsticks in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a freezer‑safe bag for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of at least 74 °C before serving.
